### The laws this wave paid for

* **A dependency edge is not a draw call.** Four links of a five-link chain
  proved, in four separate places, and the fifth — the only one a player can see
  — assumed. The gate that covered it asserted pack membership, which is the
  fourth link over again. *When a clause's title is about what the world looks
  like, at least one arm has to be about what the world looks like.*
* **A tolerance chosen for plausibility is not a tolerance chosen for a defect.**
  `mb * 0.5` was a sensible-looking number that missed the wave's own finding by
  0.85 of a level. A tolerance is only worth its place if somebody has run the
  mutation it exists to catch and written the margin down.
* **An opt-in gate is not a gate.** `INF_GOLDEN_STRICT` is set by people, not by
  CI, so a pin that only strict mode holds is a pin that holds on the days
  somebody remembers.
* **A two-point solve reconstructs its own two points.** Presenting that as a
  check is an inference wearing a measurement's clothes — the house law, met by
  the very ledger that quotes it five times.
* **Quote the denominator or the percentage is a different number.** 35.9 % of
  the map is sand; ~4.6 % of the *land* is.
* **A cost headline belongs to the configuration that ships.** +7.2 % of a lit
  frame and +100 % of a shipped one are the same change measured where it hides
  and where it does not.

---

## Wave TER2b — the ground gets its shape (2026-08-26)

Base `17c47da6`. Two things were true of the island's ground and neither was
visible from its own ledger. The three pieces of ground cover TER2a authored,
byte-locked and cooked were **not drawn** — the wave shipped 16 771 tinted cubes
and its own audit said so. And the ground under six metres was not merely coarse
but **empty**: a z15 terrarium pixel is 3.11 m at 49.34 N, a raster at that pitch
cannot represent a feature shorter than 6.23 m, and every metre below that line
was a bilinear plane through four survey samples.

Both are closed. The cover draws its authored meshes, the empty band carries
designed relief that says so, and the render mesh went from eight metres a vertex
to four.

### Clause 0 — the scattered cover draws its meshes

The TER2a audit's HIGH, and it was a five-link chain with the fifth link
assumed. Four links were real — the props are generated, byte-locked, committed,
cooked and reachable in the pack, and the audit re-verified each — and the fifth,
*anything draws them*, was false.

**The GUID had to survive evaluation, and an index could not have.**
`inf_pcg::PcgKind::mesh` was read by the packager's dependency closure and by
nothing on the draw path; `rules::evaluate_with_in` kept a `kind_index` and threw
the GUID away. The obvious repair — carry the index and look the palette up later
— **does not work, and the reason is a finding of its own**:

| where | what it concatenates | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `rules::evaluate_with_in` | every rule of every enabled layer, `out.append`, no run boundaries | two rules' index `0` are the same `u32` and different content |
| `binding::evaluate_in` | one such list per biome graph, `out.extend`, no offset | biome 1's `0` and biome 7's `0` likewise |
| `volume::compose_volume` | scatter instances **and grammar module indices**, shifting only `inst_start` | an index may name a grass tuft or a wall panel |

So the palette is resolved where the rule that owns it is still in hand, and what
rides on the instance is the GUID, which is global by construction.
`inf_pcg::PcgInstance` and its dependency-light ECS mirror
`inf_ecs::components::ScatteredInstance` each grew one `Option<Uuid>` — and
**both containers are `#[serde(skip)]` derived caches** (`PcgVolume::evaluated`
and `Terrain::biome_population`), so no schema moved in either codec mirror.

*The island dodged the collision only incidentally*: every biome in its set names
the **same** graph GUID, and that graph is one layer of one rule of three kinds,
so `0/1/2` happened to be unambiguous. That is a fact about this island, not
about the engine.

**The renderer needed a payload, not a pipeline.** The P18.5 scatter raster does
not bind a vertex buffer at all: it reads `vertices[idx * 6u + k]` and
`indices[...]` out of two storage buffers and takes its draw count from an
indirect args block the cull compute wrote. So an authored mesh is the same two
flat arrays `PrimStorage` already holds for the five built-ins.
`inf_render::ScatterGeometry` is those arrays plus a unit bounding radius and an
`xxh3` content key, `ScatterData::key` folds that key in — so the same placements
drawn as two different meshes are two payloads and the same mesh scattered twice
is one upload — and `ScatterNode` grew a `geoms` map keyed on it, retained to the
frame's live set exactly as the instance uploads are.

**The cube did not leave; it became the proxy, and that is a stated bound.**
`PrimMesh::Cube` is still passed and is still what three paths draw: the impostor
card, the CPU fallback and the cascade shadow-caster pack. All three bind **one**
shared vertex buffer for the whole frame, so a per-batch mesh does not fit in
them; widening that is a wave, and it is in the carried list. The impostor is at
least *sized* correctly now — `material.w` carries the authored unit radius and
`impostor_radius` branches on it, because a 0.307 m grass tuft at instance scale
1.0 was taking the unit cube's `0.866` and getting a billboard almost three times
its own height.

**One door, two hosts.** `ScatterGeometry::from_streams` takes exactly what
`inf_mesh::MeshAsset::vgeom_streams` produces, so the flattening, the radius and
the key are one piece of code. `MAX_SCATTER_MESH_TRIANGLES` (4 096) lives in
Ring 0 for the same reason — a mesh the editor draws and a shipped build refuses
is the divergence the projector-mirror gate exists to prevent, one level up. The
ceiling is a ceiling and not a quality knob: scatter draws its geometry *per
instance* with no meshlet LOD behind it, so 16 771 instances at 4 096 triangles
would be **68.7 M** triangles before culling, against the 10 M-triangle scene P13
gated at 2.4 % cull. The three props are 32, 20 and 128.

The two loaders are demand-shaped rather than exhaustive: they enumerate the
`.inf_pcg` documents and take the GUIDs their kinds name, because a pack's meshes
are mostly not scatter kinds and uploading a character's body to a storage buffer
at boot would cost megabytes to draw nothing. The player builds its table once at
level load (`scatter_mesh::{from_pack, from_dir}`) because a projection runs
every frame and must not open a file; the editor builds its table at the head of
each projection, which is per *document version*, from the GUIDs the evaluated
instances carry.

**The tripwire went red in the strongest form it named.** The TER2a audit's
`the_cover_meshes_are_shipped_and_are_not_yet_drawn` pinned `PcgInstance` and
`ScatteredInstance` **field by field as struct literals**, and wrote down why:
*"the day either grows a mesh reference this stops compiling, which is the
strongest form this pin can take."* It stopped compiling. It is replaced by
`the_scattered_cover_draws_its_authored_meshes`, which does what the arm it
replaces could not: it cooks the island, boots the shipping sim, drives it until
the ground is resident and the cover has scattered, and projects the result
through `project_scene_full` — the function the windowed player calls — with the
table `load_scatter_meshes` builds at boot.

| the fixture island, through the shipped door | |
|---|---|
| `grass tuft` | 32 triangles, 64 vertices, r = 0.338 m |
| `shrub` | 20 triangles, 32 vertices, r = 0.754 m |
| `rock` | 128 triangles, 384 vertices, r = 0.328 m |
| instances placed on the drive | **14 643** |
| batches carrying geometry | **3**, three **distinct** uploads |
| the same projection under an **empty** table | **1** batch, no geometry |

That last row is the anti-vacuity half and it is the pre-TER2b engine exactly.
An arm that could not tell those two apart would be measuring nothing. Every
batch's cull radius is asserted to be its **own** geometry's rather than the
proxy's — the one place the proxy must not be used, because a radius that is too
small deletes instances at the frustum edge — and the proxy is asserted to still
be a cube, so the carried bound cannot quietly become something else.

`veg_digest`, the fold `pie_equals_shipping_on_an_island_drive` compares the two
hosts on, now folds the mesh GUID beside the position and the kind. Two
populations that agree on every position and differ on which prop stands there
are two different worlds, and before this line the fold could not tell them
apart.

### Clause 1 — the recipe detail stage

`BuildStep::Detail`, between **Roads** and **Pyramid**. `BuildStep::ALL` is ten.

**What the band is, and why it is derived rather than authored.** The
`source.upsampled` advisory has said since wave I7 that detail below the source
pitch is "interpolation plus whatever the design puts there". The precise shape
of that interpolation is bilinear, and bilinear interpolation of a 3.11 m raster
contains **nothing** between 2 m (the world grid's own Nyquist) and 6.23 m (the
source's). `DetailBand::of` takes the two pitches the plan already carries and
answers a base wavelength at the source's Nyquist, a finest octave that never
crosses the grid's, and an octave count arrived at **by halving** — `log2` is on
the libm ban list and this stage writes committed bytes.

There is **no recipe field** for any of it, and that was priced before it was
decided rather than after. `IslandRecipe` is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` with
an **exact-equality** `schema_version` check and **no migrate function**, so a
v2 → v3 bump refuses every committed recipe on disk until each is hand-edited —
for three numbers that are a pure function of two the recipe already states. The
recipe schema stays **v2**. The seed is the recipe's own, salted so the band is
not a scaled copy of any other hashed decision the build makes.

`UPSAMPLE_ADVISORY_RATIO` is one constant with two readers now — the advisory and
the band — because a build that says "detail below X is the design's" and adds
none, and one that adds detail and never says so, are the same defect either way
round.

**Why that slot and no other.**

| step | why the detail must be after / before it |
|---|---|
| Roads | `roads::grade_audit` and `roads::build_mesh` are **both** built up there against `data.height_at`, so nothing this stage writes can move either |
| Hydrology | the stream network, the lakes and the committed-layer drift comparison are derived three steps earlier and are untouched |
| Pyramid | built from `data` immediately after, so the coarse levels see the ground the world actually has rather than disagreeing with level 0 |

**Four exclusions, and every one is a fade.** A hard mask edge is a visible
crease, and a crease along every road is worse than no detail at all: the shore
band (six metres, clearing both the 2.5 m coastline tolerance and the beach's own
rise), the road corridor, the stream channels and the site pads, each dead inside
its own half-width and fully detailed one width outside it, on a `t·t·(3−2t)`
ramp so the derivative a shading normal reads is continuous at both ends.
`corridor_index` is one door with two callers — the carve builds it from the
*committed* routes because it runs before the planner, the detail stage from the
*final* ones, which differ exactly when `--replan-roads` moved them.

> **CORRECTED BY THE AUDIT (HIGH-1).** Two of the four were **cuts** as this wave
> shipped them: `SegmentIndex::new`'s second argument is the index's *reach*, and
> the build passed the corridor's and the channel's own half-widths — so
> `nearest` answered `None` one micron past the mask, `segment_weight` read that
> as "take all the detail", and the ramp's input never left the interval where
> the ramp is zero. **0.0000 m of relief at 7 m from a corridor centreline and
> 0.1274 m at 8 m**, where the ramp asks for 0.007. Fixed by
> `detail::fade_reach_m`; the paragraph above is true now. Two callers, **two
> reaches**, and the carve keeps the half-width.

The amplitude is `1.5 m × (0.10 + 0.90 · slope_ramp(3°..35°)) × biome × mask`, so
a ploughed field takes a quarter of what an alpine scree face does and a flat
plain still gets **ten and a half centimetres** of undulation — a dead-flat plain
being the one thing real ground never is. (Fifteen in the first draft: the
`biome` term applies to a plain too, and its least-specific arm is 0.7. Measured
peak on a flat two-tile fixture: **0.086 m**, because a two-octave fBm does not
reach its own bound.)

**Measured on the CI fixture** (a 2 m grid over a 12.45 m z13 pixel — a 6.22×
upsample, so a wider band than the shipped island's), after the audit's two
repairs:

```
[   detail] 362636 of 599076 samples took designed relief in a 6.22..24.89 m band
           (3 octaves); mean 0.059 m, worst 1.315 m; excluded 213984 water,
           7535 corridor, 1647 channel, 13274 pad
```

The wave's own line read `mean 0.060 m` and is otherwise identical to the digit:
restoring the fade band is the whole difference, and it moves nothing else —
which is the shape a mask repair should have.

**Every fixture arm holds, and one is new.** `two_builds_of_one_recipe_produce_the_same_terrain`
is green — the stage is a pure function of `(seed, band, world position)` and its
masks. The shoreline reads **0.0038 m** from the waterline over sixteen coastline
vertices; the start gap is **0.008 m**, unmoved; the step list is frozen at ten
in order, and the log carries exactly one line per step.

The new arm is the one that could not have existed before: `grade_audit` runs
*inside* the Roads step, one step before the detail is written, so the audit the
report carries could not have seen a corridor mask that leaked however badly it
leaked. `the_detail_band_fills_the_gap_under_the_survey_and_moves_nothing_designed`
**re-runs the identical audit** against `b.terrain` — the ground as the build
finished it — and demands the same answer to the last bit: **worst grade
0.099370 against 0.099370, `to_bits`-equal, 144 stretches against 144, zero over
against zero.** Mutation-verified: `corridor: None` fails it by name.

It also asserts both ends of the band against the plan's own pitches — the base
octave no coarser than the source's Nyquist (that would be overwriting survey)
and the finest no finer than the grid's (that would be aliasing) — and reads the
worst displacement out of the ledger line rather than re-deriving it, because
what the ledger prints is what a reader trusts.

**The advisory says what it now means**: *"a feature shorter than 6.23 m is not
in the survey at all and everything below it is DESIGNED detail: the carve, the
road corridors, the stream channels, and the fBm detail band the `detail` step
writes into exactly that gap. It is not survey, and it is no longer bilinear
either."*

**Two laws paid for themselves inside this clause.** `inf-island`'s libm-ban
table went red on the first run because `detail.rs` had not joined it — the
second time this campaign the table has caught a new module unprompted. And the
workspace's eaten-`\` gate fired **twice** on this wave's own scripted edits, in
`build.rs` and in `render_assets.rs`: catches **thirty and thirty-one**, both
runs of eighteen spaces inside user-facing literals, both from a non-raw Python
string eating the Rust continuation. The remedy is the one the gate's own doc
gives: `chr(92)` or an unquoted heredoc, and neither of these two used one.

*And a third time for the libm table, inside the audit's own repair*: the first
draft of `a_shared_tile_edge_takes_one_displacement` printed its ramp angle as
`grad.atan().to_degrees()` in an assertion message, and `inf-island`'s table
reads test lines too. Caught on the first battery, before a single number was
written down. The arm carries gradients and their degrees as a pair now.

### Clause 2 — the mesh reaches the survey

`TERRAIN_BASE_CELLS` **32 → 64**: the finest clipmap ring goes from **8 m a
vertex to 4 m** over a 256 m tile, against height data at 1 m a sample.

**The A/B, on a third tree.** TER2a solved the vertex/fragment split at its base
commit and its audit re-ran the whole experiment on the shipped tree, where the
fragment half was a third dearer, and got the same verdict — 7.5 % vertex,
92.5 % fragment. It told TER2b to plan with **+0.569 ms of terrain and +0.499 ms
of a 9.051 ms frame**. This is the third tree, and it carries both of the changes
above: real scatter geometry and a rewritten heightfield.

| configuration | terrain @ 32 | terrain @ 64 | delta | GPU frame @ 32 | @ 64 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SHIPPED` | 1.780 ms | 2.086 ms | **+0.306 (+17.2 %)** | 2.391 | 2.676 | +0.285 |
| `LIT` | 2.535 | 3.122 | +0.587 (+23.2 %) | 8.961 | 9.465 | +0.504 |
| `LIT+SSR` | 2.535 | 3.120 | +0.585 (+23.1 %) | 8.991 | 9.480 | +0.489 |
| **`LIT+VIS`** | **2.535** | **3.122** | **+0.587 (+23.2 %)** | **9.084** | **9.561** | **+0.477** |
| `LIT-COARSE-CLIPMAP` | 2.593 | 3.184 | +0.591 (+22.8 %) | 5.188 | 5.798 | +0.610 |
| p50 (`LIT+VIS`) | 13.962 ms (71.6 fps) | **14.499 ms (69.0 fps)** | −2.6 fps | | | |

**The prediction reproduces**: +0.587 measured against +0.569 predicted for the
terrain pass, +0.477 against +0.499 for the frame. **≥ 60 fps p50 `LIT+VIS` with
everything on: MET at 69.0 fps**, with 2.10 ms of p50 headroom and 7.04 ms of GPU
headroom against a 16.6 ms frame.

**And the delta is NOT a constant number of milliseconds** — which is a
correction to how "+0.569 ms" reads, and this wave's own contribution to the
split TER2a measured. The same doubling costs **+0.306 ms in `SHIPPED` and
+0.587 in `LIT`**, nearly twice, so it is not a fixed vertex cost sitting beside
an unchanged fragment half. A finer mesh packs smaller triangles into the same
2×2 quads, and that extra quad work is dearer exactly where a fragment is
dearer. TER2a's ledger listed this as its second *unverified* assumption in as
many words — *"the sign of the error is that the finer mesh pays a little more
fragment time"* — and it is measured now rather than assumed. The consequence
for a reader: the density's price is a fraction of the terrain pass (≈ 22 %),
not a millisecond figure that travels between configurations.

**Nothing else moved with it, and each is a reason rather than a hope.**
`lod_thresholds` is a function of the tile span and `TERRAIN_LOD_SCALE` alone, so
the ring radii are unchanged. `patch_mesh_lod`'s ring↔asset-LOD pairing is a
difference of two indices and knows nothing about density. And the skirt is
`max(|hmax − hmin|, 0.05 · span, 1 m)` — a function of a tile's own span and
height **range**, not of its cell count — so it is the same wall it was. Seams
seal by construction and get *safer*: the module header's argument is that either
side's skirt already spans the worst-case gap between two LODs, and a finer fine
side deviates from the coarse one by **less**. The `cells_at_lod` table is
re-blessed 32/16/8/4 → 64/32/16/8, with a derived arm beside the four literals so
the next raise moves one constant and nothing else.

**The goldens, measured rather than assumed.** `INF_GOLDEN_STRICT=1` is green
over all 58 with the density raise and no committed image moved — which looked
like the raise reaching no golden at all, so it was checked rather than believed.
A blessing run moves **thirteen** images (`terrain`, `terrain_lod`,
`terrain_splat`, `gi_terrain`, `ground_close`, `cave_mouth`, `biomes`, `deform`
and the five `water_*` scenes), and **every one of them sits inside the strict
tolerance**. So the raise does reach them, the strict gate cannot see it, and
**none is re-blessed**: the TER2a precedent exactly (*"the committed image did
not have to move because the change sits inside the strict tolerance, but the
statistic did"*). Goldens stay **58**, `git diff` over `tests/goldens` is empty.

### Clause 3 — parallax occlusion mapping: ROUTED, and priced

Not taken. Three prices, and the first is fatal on its own.

1. **There is nothing to march.** `inf_material::MaterialAsset` carries
   `base_color_texture`, `normal_texture`, `metallic_roughness_texture` and
   `detail_texture` — and **no height or displacement slot**. POM ray-marches a
   height field; adding one is an `.inf_mat` schema move, which is an *engine*
   schema and is out of this wave's bounds by rule.
2. **The atlas would demote.** TER2a measured that `build_vt_level` reads the
   pool format off the *stored* formats of the textures a level binds and a
   **mixed** set drops the whole pool to `Rgba8`: 73 984 B a page against BC1's
   9 248, so a 24 MiB pool holds **340** pages instead of 2 721. A single-channel
   height map beside four BC1 maps is exactly such a set unless it is authored
   BC1 — a three-channel format carrying one channel.
3. **It spends in the dominant half, which this wave just made dearer.** The
   pass is 92.5 % fragment-bound and clause 2 raised it 23 %. A per-fragment ray
   march of 8–32 taps is the single most expensive place in this frame to put new
   work, and the headroom it would eat is the 7.04 ms clause 2 left.

The door stays open (there is no ruling against tessellation, POM or
displacement). What it wants first is a height channel in the material schema and
a second VT pool — both of which are the *same* wave as routed item 1 of TER2a's
list.

### Clause 4 — erosion-informed micro-detail: ROUTED, and priced

Not taken. The P10 CPU erosion sim (`inf_terrain::erosion`, three `sqrt` calls,
exact conservation, the CPU tier being the golden because the GPU one is not
portable) would run on the detail band at recipe time.

**The committed-water consequence, stated as the brief asks.** Erosion moves
material to make channels. The island's stream network, its lakes and its
committed-layer **drift comparison** are all derived at `BuildStep::Hydrology`,
three steps before the detail slot, from the *pre-detail* heights. So:

* erosion **in** the detail slot cuts channels the committed streams do not
  follow — the world would have watercourses with no water in them and water in
  places with no watercourse;
* erosion **before** the hydrology step rewrites the committed water design,
  which is already drifting **16.47 %** in lake area against a fresh derivation,
  and that layer is what the level ships.

Either placement is a wave with the water design in its scope, not a stage that
can be slotted in beside the fBm. The second price is the build: 51.4 million
level-0 samples through an iterative droplet sim, on the byte-identity path, on
every build.

### The island, before and after

`the_island_at_shipping_resolution`, same machine (RTX 4070 Ti, **release**,
1080p, 3 × 120 frames, MIN of rounds), the same 51.38 km² island. "Before" is the
TER2a **audit's** own re-run at `17c47da6`, which is this wave's base.

**`LIT+VIS` — everything on.**

| | before (`17c47da6`) | clauses 0 + 1 | **after TER2b** |
|---|---|---|---|
| p50 | 13.522 ms (74.0 fps) | 13.962 (71.6) | **14.499 ms (69.0 fps)** |
| GPU frame | 8.951–9.051 ms | 9.084 | **9.561 ms** |
| `terrain` | 2.515 ms | 2.535 | **3.122 ms** |
| `scatter` | 0.131 ms | 0.139 | **0.140 ms** |
| `vsm-raster` | 4.485–4.499 | — | 4.485 |
| scatter **batches** | 1 | 3 | **3** |
| scattered instances | 16 771 | 16 771 | **16 771** |
| virtual textures | 14 | 14 | **14** |
| ring-0 mesh pitch | 8 m/vertex | 8 | **4 m/vertex** |

**`SHIPPED` — the configuration that ships.**

| | before (`17c47da6`) | clauses 0 + 1 | **after TER2b** |
|---|---|---|---|
| p50 | 5.421 ms (184.5 fps) | 6.037 (165.7) | **6.236 ms (160.3 fps)** |
| GPU frame | 2.244 ms | 2.391 | **2.676 ms** |
| `terrain` | 1.667 ms | 1.780 | **2.086 ms** |
| terrain's share | 74 % | 74 % | **78 %** |
| `scatter` | 0.131 ms | 0.141 | **0.136 ms** |
| against `SHIPPING_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` (16.6) | 33 % | 36 % | **38 %** |

**Both tables, because one of them hides the cost.** TER2a's audit made this a
rule: a lit frame has 4.5 ms of `vsm-raster` to hide a terrain pass behind and a
shipped one has nothing, so the honest headline is two numbers. **The whole wave
costs the lit island +0.510 ms of GPU frame (+5.6 %) and the shipped island
+0.432 ms (+19.3 %)**, and terrain's share of the shipped frame went 74 % → 78 %.
Nothing breaches: 6.236 ms is 38 % of the shipping budget.

**Two things worth not over-reading.**

*The cover meshes are free.* The `scatter` pass drew 16 771 tinted **cubes** at
0.131 ms and now draws 16 771 **authored meshes** — 32, 20 and 128 triangles
against a cube's 12 — at 0.140 ms, in three batches instead of one. **+0.009 ms
for roughly five times the geometry and two extra draws.** That is the P18.5 GPU
scatter path doing what it was built for, and it is the same shape as TER2a's own
"6.25× the instances for +0.006 ms".

*The clause-0-and-1 half is not cleanly attributable.* The middle column moved
the shipped terrain +0.113 ms and the lit terrain +0.020, and those two runs
differ in **both** the scatter geometry and the heightfield — a rougher ground
changes what faces the camera and what early-Z rejects. Which of the two it is
would need a fourth run nobody has taken. The A/B that *is* clean is clause 2's:
one tree, one constant, two values (the TER2a derivative-lane precedent, met
again and named the same way).

### Routed, not taken — by name

1. **POM / tessellation / displacement on the terrain fragment path.** Clause 3
   above, with its three prices. It wants a height channel in `MaterialAsset` and
   a second VT pool before it wants a ray march.
2. **Erosion-informed micro-detail.** Clause 4 above, with the committed-water
   consequence of both possible placements.
3. **A windowed PIE session still draws the cover as placeholder cubes.** The
   fourth instance of a class this engine has closed three times — P21.4 for
   voxel volumes, P24.1 for skeletal meshes, P26.4 for materials — and each of
   those three left a comment saying it was *"passed in rather than defaulted so
   the gap cannot reopen silently"*. `run_pie` has no scatter-mesh table, so
   `--pie` falls back to the placeholder path while a cooked boot draws meshes.
   The **fix needs no schema move**: `ScenePayload::meshes` is already a general
   `Vec<(Uuid, Vec<u8>)>` of `.inf_mesh` bytes that only `SkeletalMesh.mesh`
   fills today, so adding the scatter kinds to it is a *use* of a field. Named
   here rather than taken because this wave's slice closed at three clauses.
   `pie_equals_shipping_on_an_island_drive` is unaffected and green — it compares
   **simulation** state, and its vegetation fold now carries the mesh GUID.
   **Named at `run_pie` since the audit** (LOW-1): the three comments closing
   P21.4, P24.1 and P26.4 sit on consecutive lines there and the open fourth was
   not among them, and that function is the one place a reader looks to find out
   which of the class are shut.
4. **The scatter proxy: impostors, the CPU fallback and cascade shadow casters
   still draw a cube.** All three bind one shared vertex buffer for the whole
   frame, so a per-batch mesh does not fit in them; the fix is a shared scatter
   geometry *atlas* with per-kind ranges, which changes `pack_fallback`'s
   `[Range<u32>; 5]` return and the shadow node's `CasterKey` with it. The
   impostor at least sizes its card off the authored radius now.
5. **A scattered mesh is tinted, not textured.** The scatter pull buffer is
   `SCATTER_PULL_STRIDE = 6` — position then normal — and carries **no uv**, so
   there is nowhere for a material to be sampled. The three cover props each name
   a ground material in their sidecar and the cook ships the two together, and
   that edge is still a dependency edge and not a texel. Widening the stride to 8
   and giving `ScatterBatch` a `VtTextureSet` is the wave.
6. **A scatter kind's mesh has no LOD band and no alpha cut-out.** What comes
   after item 5, not instead of it.
7. **Decal renderer** (own wave); **LiDAR gridding** (a new source kind);
   **coarse-LOD hole propagation**; **filtered outer-ring pyramid** — all four
   routed by the TER2 brief itself and untouched here.

### Carried, by name

1. **`kind_index` collides across rules, layers, biome graphs and grammar
   modules.** Clause 0 routed *around* it — the GUID is what the draw path reads
   now — but the index itself is still a `u32` that means different things in
   different runs of one list, and `pcg_kind_color` still tints from it. On this
   island that is invisible (one graph, one rule, three kinds). On a world with
   two scatter rules it is two kinds sharing a colour. The fix is a global
   palette with per-run offsets, and it is a wave.
2. **Coarse LOD pages shade off layer 0's colour** — TER2a's carried item 1,
   untouched. Weights are not carried above L0, so a distant page is
   grass-coloured rather than the blend of what is there. Clause 2 makes it
   *slightly* more visible by pulling the LOD-0 ring's detail up without touching
   the outer rings.
3. **The detail band does not reach the pyramid's own coarse levels as detail.**
   It is written into level 0 before `build_asset`, so the coarse levels are a
   *decimation* of detailed ground rather than ground with detail of their own —
   correct, and the only honest thing a pyramid can do, but it means the band is
   invisible past the LOD-0 ring.
4. **Ground cover still stops at ~1.3 km² around the player** (`SIM_MARGIN_TILES`
   2.0) while the renderer draws terrain to the horizon. TER2a's routed item 4,
   untouched: now that the cover is real geometry rather than cubes, the edge is
   more visible, not less.
5. ~~**The detail band's slope term reads a tile's neighbours across a border
   after the neighbour may already have been written.** … by the amount a soft
   32°-wide amplitude ramp moves — fractions of a millimetre.~~
   **STRUCK BY THE AUDIT (HIGH-2), AND IT WAS NOT A FRACTION OF A MILLIMETRE.**
   Measured at **0.382 m on a 20° slope and 0.498 m on 35°** — a crack in the
   committed heightfield, because adjacent tiles *share* a row of samples and the
   two copies took different displacements. `apply_detail` is two passes now: the
   rim is settled for every tile before any tile is written, so both copies of a
   shared sample are computed from identical neighbourhoods and are identical to
   the bit. Armed by `a_shared_tile_edge_takes_one_displacement`.
6. **Thirteen goldens move under a blessing run and none is re-blessed**, because
   every one is inside the strict tolerance. The next wave that touches terrain
   shading will move them out of it, and that will be a stated-purpose re-bless.
7. **`MAX_SCATTER_MESH_TRIANGLES` is a refusal with no author-facing surface.** A
   scatter kind naming a 5 000-triangle prop falls back to a placeholder cube
   with a `tracing::warn!` and nothing in the editor says so. The same shape as
   the `[vgeom] min_triangles` placeholder P23 carried.

### Commits

`102162b5` the ground cover stops being sixteen thousand cubes (clause 0);
`ee5da881` the ground below six metres stops being a plane through four samples
(clause 1); `4d80a930` eight metres a vertex over one-metre data becomes four
(clause 2); plus the ledger commit that carries this section into the memo and
the ROADMAP.

### The laws this wave paid for

* **A dependency edge is not a draw call, and a GUID that dies at evaluation is
  not a binding.** TER2a proved four links of a five-link chain in four separate
  places and assumed the fifth. What made the repair possible was not adding a
  field but noticing that the *index* could never have carried the answer:
  `kind_index` is rule-local and every list that concatenates populations
  concatenates it without offsetting. An identity that is only unique inside the
  scope that minted it is not an identity.
* **A tripwire written to stop compiling is worth three written to fail.** The
  TER2a audit pinned two records field by field precisely so that growing a mesh
  reference would break the build rather than a `contains`. It did, on the first
  `cargo check`, before a single test ran.
* **Price a schema bump against what it invalidates, not against what it costs to
  write.** The recipe fields for the detail band would have been three lines.
  What stopped them is that `IslandRecipe` has an exact-equality version check
  and no migrate function, so v3 refuses every committed recipe on disk — for
  numbers derivable from two the recipe already states.
* **Put a stage where nothing measured can move, then re-measure it anyway.** The
  detail slot was chosen so the road grade audit could not see it; the new arm
  runs that audit a second time, on the finished ground, *because* the first one
  could not.
* **A cost measured in milliseconds does not travel between configurations.** The
  same density doubling is +0.306 ms shipped and +0.587 ms lit. TER2a wrote the
  assumption down as unverified; verifying it turned a number into a fraction.
* **"The gate is green" and "nothing moved" are different claims.** Thirteen
  goldens move under this wave and the strict gate cannot see any of them.
  Blessing and reverting is how that was learned, and it cost one run.

## Wave TER2b — the adversarial audit (2026-08-26)

Range `17c47da6..9513c3ca`, four commits, on a clean tree. **Two HIGH, three MED,
seven LOW.** Both HIGHs and all three MEDs are fixed with arms behind them; the
LOWs are corrected in place above or carried by name. Nothing in the wave was
reverted, and none of the three clauses' headline claims was found to be false at
the level it was measured.

**The wave's arithmetic is sound and its measurements reproduce.** Every frame
number, coverage percentage and fixture count re-ran to the printed decimal, the
VT-pool and triangle-ceiling prices check out against the code they cite, and the
wave's two self-corrections — that a millisecond cost does not travel between
configurations, and that thirteen goldens move under a blessing run the strict
gate cannot see — are the kind this campaign exists to produce.

**What the audit found is two seams in the ground the detail stage writes.** One
runs along every road and every stream bed; one runs down every tile border. Both
are things clause 1's own prose says cannot be there, and one of them the wave's
carried list quantified at a **thousandth** of its measured size.

### HIGH-1 — every mask is called a fade and two of the four were CUTS

*Fixed; `21922f2a`.*

Clause 1's design sentence: *"Four exclusions, and every one is a fade. A hard
mask edge is a visible crease, and a crease along every road is worse than no
detail at all."* The road corridor and the stream channels were hard cuts.

`segment_weight` ramps `0 → 1` over `[half, half·(1+FADE_WIDTHS)]` and reads a
`None` from `SegmentIndex::nearest` as **"far away, take all the detail"**. The
build handed it `SegmentIndex::new(&lines, corridor_half)` and
`channel_index(&streams, widest)` — and that second argument **is the index's
reach**. So the query answers `Some` out to exactly the half-width and `None` one
micron later, the ramp's input never leaves `[0, half]`, where the ramp is
identically zero, and the weight steps `0 → 1` in a single sample.

Measured on the world rather than argued — a 7 m corridor across a 20° ramp on a
1 m grid, displacement read out of the finished tile:

| distance from the centreline | relief written | what the ramp asks for |
|---|---|---|
| 7.0 m | **0.0000 m** | 0.000 |
| 8.0 m | **0.1274 m** | 0.007 |
| 10.0 m | 0.4320 m | 0.126 |
| 14.0 m | 0.1286 m | 0.129 |

The step at the mask edge is an arbitrary fBm draw times the **full** modulated
amplitude — up to `MAX_AMPLITUDE_M` on steep ground — repeated along every route
in the design and every stream bed. The index's own probe shows the mechanism
directly: `reach_m = 7`, `Some(7.000)` at seven metres, `None` at 7.001.

**Fixed** by `detail::fade_reach_m`, one function with the rule in its name. The
detail stage's two indices are built through it and the **carve keeps its own at
the half-width**, which is the right reach for levelling ground and is exactly
why the two cannot share one index — so `corridor_index` is still one door, and
its two callers now differ in *both* arguments rather than one. `apply_detail`
`debug_assert!`s the invariant for both indices, and every CI leg builds the
fixture island in `dev`, so a build that regresses the reach fails loudly.

Mutation-verified in both directions inside one arm:
`a_mask_index_must_answer_past_the_fade_or_the_fade_is_a_cut` builds **both**
indices and keeps the defect as its control — `0.0` at the half-width and `1.0`
one metre later — then walks the fixed one in centimetres and demands no step
above 0.01. Beside it, `a_short_corridor_index_is_refused_rather_than_cut` is a
`should_panic` arm on the guard itself, because the defect lived in the *wiring*
and a rule with no wiring check is how it got there.

Cost to the fixture: the exclusion counts do not move at all (213 984 water,
7 535 corridor, 1 647 channel, 13 274 pad — identical), the worst displacement
does not move (1.315 m), the sample count does not move (362 636 of 599 076), and
the mean falls **0.060 → 0.059 m**. Restoring a fade band should move the mean and
nothing else, and it did.

### HIGH-2 — a shared tile edge took two different displacements

*Fixed; `21922f2a`.*

The wave's carried item 5: *"across a border it can, by the amount a soft 32°-wide
amplitude ramp moves — **fractions of a millimetre**."*

It is **0.382 m on a 20° slope and 0.498 m on a 35° one** — three orders of
magnitude out, and not a rounding remark but a **crack in the committed
heightfield**.

The note has the mechanism right and the magnitude wrong. Adjacent tiles *share* a
row of samples (`tile_span = (res − 1) · mps`), so one metre of ground is stored
twice. The one-pass walk wrote tile A, then computed tile B's rim amplitude from a
central difference reading A — now displaced by up to the full amplitude one metre
away, which moves the measured slope by tens of degrees, which moves `shape` from
0.10 toward 1.0, which multiplies the amplitude by up to seven. The two copies of
one sample then disagree by most of an amplitude.

On the island that is **784 tiles, 1 512 shared edges, 388 k duplicated samples**,
every one free to disagree. The *visual* half is largely covered by the skirt —
`max(|hmax − hmin|, 0.05·span, 1 m)`, always at least a metre, which is why
nothing caught it by looking — but `TerrainData::height_at` resolves a boundary to
the `+X/+Z` tile, so the **ground query** steps by up to half a metre as a
character crosses a tile line, and the per-tile heightfield colliders carry the
same step.

**Fixed** by making `apply_detail` two passes over one settled ground. Pass one
computes the **rim** — `is_rim`, the only samples whose central difference leaves
the tile, because an interior sample at `i = 1` reads `i = 0` and `i = 2` and both
are its own — for every tile while nothing has moved. Pass two computes the
interiors, which cannot reach out of their tile at all, and spends pass one's
answers. Both copies of a shared sample are therefore computed from identical
neighbourhoods and are identical to the bit. The refactor lifts the per-sample
decision into one `outcome_at`, so a sample computed in one pass and spent in
another cannot be counted twice in the stats.

Mutation-verified: forcing pass two to recompute the rim — the one-pass engine
exactly — fails `a_shared_tile_edge_takes_one_displacement` by name, at 0.0179 m
on the *gentlest* of its four ramps. The arm carries its own anti-vacuity half:
the stage must have moved that fixture by more than the tolerance it then demands
zero of. The "fractions of a millimetre" sentence is replaced by the measurement,
on `apply_detail` itself.

### MED-3 — a cited pin that could not fail, and never called what it named

*Fixed; `21922f2a`.* `detail::slope_deg_at`'s header said the two slope rules "are
pinned against each other by `tests::the_slope_rule_agrees_with_the_splat_walk`".
That test never called `splat::slope_deg_at`. What it asserted is that a 30° ramp
measures 30°, which is a fact about `patan2_64` that the splat walk is not needed
for and **cannot** falsify — the TER2a-audit law (*a cited gate that does not
exist is worse than no claim*) met inside the wave that quotes it.

`splat::slope_deg_at` is `pub(crate)` now, with the reason on it, and the arm
compares **both** implementations over every sample of two tiles — 162 samples,
rim included, `to_bits`-equal — which is where the two differ most (`splat` reads
its own tile's buffer for interior samples and `height_at` across a border;
`detail` goes through `height_at` for all four). The old assertions are kept as
its tail.

### MED-4 — a doc comment slid onto the wrong function

*Fixed; `f7605ced`.* Clause 0 inserted `sync_scatter_meshes` **between**
`sync_vt_bindings`'s forty-line doc comment and `sync_vt_bindings` itself. It
compiles, rustdoc renders it, nothing warns — and the P26.4/P26.5 finding
(*"nothing in the codebase ever cleared the binding set"*, with the two tests that
now hold it) became the header of a wave-TER2b scatter walk, while the function it
was written about was left undocumented.

Put back, with a line saying what happened, because a doc block that slides is
silent in a way a moved function is not.

### MED-5 — the editor's negative cache was thrown away every projection

*Fixed; `f7605ced`.* `sync_scatter_meshes`'s own doc says the loads "happen once
each, because `resolve_scatter_geometry` caches its misses as well as its hits".
It does — and the live-asset audit two hundred lines later read
`self.scatter_meshes.keys()`, which holds only the **hits**, so `retain_only`
evicted every miss on the very projection that took it.

The consequence lands on the wave's own carried item 7: a scatter kind naming a
prop past `MAX_SCATTER_MESH_TRIANGLES` re-opened and re-decoded that `.inf_mesh`
on **every document version**, which during a gizmo drag is once per input event.
The audit is keyed on what the instances *named* now (`scatter_wanted`) — the
question rather than the answer.

### The LOWs, corrected in place

1. **`run_pie` names three closed gaps and not the open fourth.** The wave's
   loudest carried item — *a windowed PIE session still draws the cover as
   placeholder cubes, the fourth instance of the class P21.4 / P24.1 / P26.4 each
   closed* — was in the memo and the ROADMAP and **not at `run_pie`**, where the
   three comments closing the other three sit on consecutive lines and where a
   reader goes to find out which are open. Written there now, with the
   no-schema-move route and with why the PIE gate cannot see it.
2. **The recipe-bump pricing was not where the next recipe bump will look.**
   Clause 1's best decision — v3 refuses every committed recipe because the check
   is exact equality and there is no migrate function — lived in `detail.rs`'s
   module doc and in the memo. It is on `RECIPE_SCHEMA_VERSION` now, with the rule
   the next author needs: *bump it when a recipe must state something it cannot
   derive, and add a migrate function in the same commit, or the bump is a
   breaking change wearing a version number.*
3. **"A flat plain still gets fifteen centimetres."** It gets **10.5 cm**:
   `AMPLITUDE_FLOOR_FRACTION × MAX_AMPLITUDE_M` is 0.15 m and then
   `biome_amplitude`'s `_` arm — which every unclassified sample takes —
   multiplies by 0.7. Measured peak on a flat two-tile fixture: **0.086 m**,
   because a two-octave fBm does not reach its own bound.
4. **"This stage fills that band" fills one octave of the 1.64 it names.** The
   empty band is 2 m → 6.23 m; octaves halve from 6.23 and stop before crossing
   the grid's Nyquist, so 3.11 m → 2 m stays exactly as empty as it was. Filling
   it would be aliasing, and
   `the_island_band_runs_from_the_sources_nyquist_to_the_grids` is the arm that
   refuses it. The module doc states the bound now.
5. **The `MIRROR-BEGIN scatter_mesh_buckets` fence has no reader.**
   `projector_mirror` compares two tags by fence (`pcg_scatter_lod`,
   `pcg_shell_batch`) and this is not one of them. Nothing is lost — the whole
   `push_scatter` body is already compared by `extract_fn`, which is strictly
   stronger — but a fence that looks like a pin and is not is the shape this
   campaign keeps paying for. Carried rather than fixed: the remedy would compare
   something already compared.
6. **"14 643 instances → 3 batches … over the real cooked island."** It is the
   **fixture** island: `island_gate::build_project` loads the fixture recipe, not
   `samples/island/island.toml`. The memo's own table says "the fixture island"
   and is right; the ROADMAP block read as the 51 km² one and now says which.
7. **The +10-arm target list names a crate that gained none.** The count is right
   — `git diff` over the range adds exactly ten `#[test]`s: seven in `detail.rs`,
   one in the fixture, two in `scatter_mesh.rs`, and `island_gate` nets zero by
   replacing its tripwire. The parenthetical also listed `inf-render`'s lib, which
   added no arm: it re-blessed `cells_halve_per_lod` and grew a derived assertion
   *inside* it.

### Carried by name, with a measurement rather than an argument

1. **Inland lakes are not in the exclusion list.** The four exclusions name the
   *sea*. A lake is inside the coastline with its bed well above sea level, so
   `is_land` is true, the shore fade is fully open, and designed relief is written
   into a bed the design has already put water on. Measured on the fixture: the
   one lake is **1.389 m deep** and its shallowest bed sample finishes **0.572 m
   under the surface** — nothing pokes through today, and the margin is *smaller*
   than the stage's own 1.5 m ceiling. A shallower lake, or a bed the classifier
   calls alpine (full amplitude rather than 0.7 of it), grows an island the design
   never drew. Not fixed, because a fifth exclusion moves committed bytes;
   **armed** by `no_lake_bed_rises_above_its_own_water_surface`, which asserts the
   right outcome and prints the margin. The day it goes red the fix is the lake's
   own outline and level, on exactly the sea's rule.
2. **The density raise is paid at every ring, not only at ring 0.**
   `lod_thresholds` is a function of the tile span and `TERRAIN_LOD_SCALE` alone,
   so the ring radii did not move and every ring took four times the triangles —
   which is what the 22.6 % is. "Ring 0 at 64 with the rings pulled in" is a
   different way to spend the same budget and was not measured.
3. **The two hosts build their scatter-mesh tables from different questions.**
   The player enumerates `.inf_pcg` documents and takes every GUID their kinds
   name; the editor walks the evaluated instances and takes the GUIDs they carry.
   The player's set is a superset, so a mesh in the pack and absent from the
   editor's content root draws in a shipped build and not in the viewport. The
   projector *body* is pinned character for character; the two table builders are
   not, and cannot be — they read different stores.

**And the real island's own detail line**, which the wave measured on the CI
fixture and never printed for the world it ships (`--dry-run`, so nothing under

```
[   detail] 37675364 of 51782416 samples took designed relief in a 3.11..6.23 m
           band (2 octaves); mean 0.093 m, worst 1.493 m; excluded 11129344
           water, 661345 corridor, 166728 channel, 2149635 pad
```

Two things a reader should take from it. **72.8 % of the island took relief**,
and its **worst displacement is 1.493 m against the stage's own 1.5 m ceiling** —
99.5 % of it, where the CI fixture only reaches 1.315 m. So the ceiling is a
real bound on the shipped world and not a theoretical one, and the fixture does
not prove it. And the corridor exclusion (661 345 samples) agrees with the
carve's own corridor count (661 290) to 0.008 %, which is what "one door, two
route lists" should look like. The advisory reads back exactly as clause 1 says
it does, with `6.23 m` in it.

### The audit's commits

`21922f2a` the detail band's two seams — a mask that cut and an edge that split
(HIGH-1, HIGH-2, MED-3, the lake arm and two LOW corrections); `f7605ced`
clause 0's three — a doc that slid, a cache thrown away, a claim with no arm
(MED-4, MED-5, the collision arm); `7b61d574` two prices stated where the next
reader will look for them (LOW-1, LOW-2); `f946b8b1` three rustdoc links the
repairs added, and the real island's own detail line; plus the ledger commit
carrying this section and the corrections above into the memo and the ROADMAP.

### What the audit did NOT find

Stated because an audit that lists only what it broke is not a reading of the
wave.

* **Clause 0 is sound end to end, and its central finding is right.** The GUID
  really is the only thing that could have worked: `kind_index` is rule-local and
  `evaluate_with_in`, `BiomeBinding::evaluate_in` and `compose_volume` all
  concatenate without offsetting it. Neither container that grew a field reaches
  a wire — `PcgInstance` has no `Serialize` derive and `Terrain::biome_population`
  is `#[serde(skip)]` in the live component *and* in `inf-scene`'s frozen
  `TerrainV23`, which the audit checked because a mirror is exactly where that
  claim would fail. Batch order is a `BTreeMap` in both hosts, so it is a function
  of the mesh set and not of a hash seed; the geometry cache is content-keyed and
  retained to the frame's live set on the same rule as the instance uploads; and
  an unresolvable GUID buckets with the meshless ones, so it degrades to the
  placeholder rather than to an empty batch.
* **"The cover meshes are free" is true and the frame agrees with it.** All five
  configurations report **3 batches / 16 771 instances / 14 virtual textures**, and
  the `scatter` pass costs 0.138–0.141 ms in every one of them — so the batches
  are not culled to nothing, and the instance count in the measured frame is the
  one the claim is about.
* **Clause 2's "nothing else moved" holds by construction, not by luck.**
  `lod_thresholds` reads the tile span and `TERRAIN_LOD_SCALE`; `patch_mesh_lod`
  is a difference of two indices; the skirt is `max(|hmax − hmin|, 0.05·span, 1 m)`
  — a tile's own span and height *range*, with no cell count in it. The patch
  index buffer is `Vec<u32>`, so 65² + skirt has no ceiling near it.
* **Both routed prices are real.** `MaterialAsset` has no height or displacement
  slot (read field by field), and `build_vt_level` genuinely drops a **mixed**
  stored-format set to `Rgba8` for the whole pool — the demotion is about the
  *set*, not about the height channel, which is the part the clause could have
  got wrong and did not.
* **The recipe-bump refusal is real.** `IslandRecipe::validate` compares
  `schema_version` for exact equality, there is no migrate function anywhere in
  the crate, and every struct is `deny_unknown_fields`.
* **The tripwire's replacement is not vacuous.** It drives the shipped
  `project_scene_full` with the table `load_scatter_meshes` builds at boot, checks
  each batch's cull radius against its *own* geometry, and its anti-vacuity half
  (the same projection under an empty table → one meshless batch) is the pre-wave
  engine exactly.
* **The `MIRROR-BEGIN scatter_mesh_buckets` region is compared** — not by that
  fence, which no gate reads, but by `extract_fn` over the whole `push_scatter`
  body, which is stronger.

### The laws this audit paid for

* **The reach of an index is part of the rule it answers.** A mask that ramps over
  `[half, 2·half]` and an index that stops at `half` are each reasonable alone and
  together are a hard cut. Neither file is wrong on its own; the defect lives in
  the argument passed between them, which is why the fix is a named function and a
  `debug_assert` rather than a corrected literal.
* **"Fractions of a millimetre" is a measurement, and it needs measuring.** The
  wave described the cross-border feedback exactly right and guessed its size
  three orders of magnitude low. An honest note about a hazard is worth less than
  the same note with a number somebody actually took.
* **A shared sample is one sample.** Wherever tiles overlap by a row, a per-sample
  walk that reads a neighbourhood is a two-pass problem, and the set that has to
  be settled first is exactly the rim.
* **A doc comment can move without moving.** Inserting a function between a header
  and its body reattaches forty lines of hard-won finding to something else, and
  no compiler, linter or rustdoc run says a word.
* **A cache is invalidated by the question, not by the answer.** Keying a live-set
  audit on what resolved throws away precisely the entries whose whole purpose is
  to remember that they did not.
* **A ceiling the fixture cannot reach is not a ceiling the fixture tests.** The
  detail band's worst displacement is 1.315 m on CI and 1.493 m on the world that
  ships — 99.5 % of its own bound. The number that matters was one `--dry-run`
  away and no wave had taken it.

## Wave I8a — the settlements exist (2026-08-27)

Base `9f6e4689`. Five clauses. Wave I7's own carried remainder 12 read: *"the
site pads are terraces, not settlements. Seven sites, 2.34 km² of levelled
ground and 5.8 % of the land reserved urban — and nothing standing on any of
it."* Something stands on all seven now: **172 blocks and 60.88 km of street**, about **1 800 buildings**, and a walk
into one of them that the shipped player and the editor's document agree on
**byte for byte**. (1 800 is a DERIVATION — 172 blocks times the furnish
battery's own measured per-archetype block counts — where the enterability
invariants are a MEASUREMENT over 42 sampled buildings and, through
`phase19_gate`, over all seven archetypes.)

**And the headline is the price.** The island went from **69.0 fps LIT+VIS to
9.4**, and the mechanism is not what the brief assumed: a settlement draws
through the P18.5 GPU **scatter** path — a foliage path — as **365 545 opaque,
wall-sized boxes** with no occlusion culling behind them. *Cubes are the
EXPENSIVE case, not the cheap one*, which is the correction this wave makes to
its own brief and the single most useful thing it hands I8b.

### Clause 1 — the settlement generator

`inf_editor_core::settlement`, Ring 1, beside `island_scene`, a **pure function
of `IslandDesign`**: the sites, the committed road routes and the coastline
rings, and no elevation anywhere in it. The building datum is resolved at
*evaluation* time from the terrain under each lot's own centre
(`Ground::Terrain`), which is the one place the ground is allowed to be asked.

```text
  site (centre, radius) ─▶ street GRID on the world axes, a line through the
                           site's own centre on both axes
                        ─▶ BLOCKS between the lines, refused when they leave the
                           reservation circle or the coastline crosses them
                        ─▶ ZONE per block (Chebyshev ring + the highway cluster)
                        ─▶ one PcgVolume naming that zone's committed `.inf_pcg`
                             ─▶ `building.lots` cuts the block into lots (IB-2c)
                             ─▶ `building.plan` stands one building on each
```

**THE ZONING TABLE.** "Districts" are deterministic rules, not a new type. A
zone is a weighted archetype list; the pick is a counter hash of the block's own
grid position, so it is a pure function of the design.

| site | ring | zone | archetypes (weights) |
|---|---|---|---|
| city | 0 | core | Office 5, Hotel 2, Shop 3 |
| city | 1 | inner | Office 3, Apartment 3, Shop 2, Hotel 1 |
| city | 2 | ring | Apartment 4, Shop 1 |
| city | ≥ 3 | edge | House 3, Estate 1 |
| city | (cluster) | industrial | Industrial — 4 blocks, ring ≥ half the depth, nearest the point the highway leaves the city |
| town | 0 | high street | Shop 3, House 1 |
| town | ≥ 1 | outskirt | House 4, Estate 1 |

**And the lot rules per archetype**, which is the other half of what a zone
means (lots on a 100 m city block, by `subdivide_block`'s own round-to-nearest
rule): Office 30 × 34 m → 9, Hotel 36 × 36 → 9, Shop 20 × 28 → 20, Apartment
26 × 30 → 12, House 18 × 26 → 24, Estate 40 × 44 → 6, Industrial 48 × 48 → 4.
`floors` is **0** — drawn from the archetype's own storey range per lot seed —
so a street of houses is one to three storeys rather than a terrace of identical
boxes.

**Two refusals, and both are VALUES.** A block whose corner leaves the
reservation circle, and a block the coastline crosses. Both are **proofs rather
than samples**:

* the pad test — a disc is convex and a rectangle is the convex hull of its
  corners, so four corners inside the circle put every *lot* the subdivider cuts
  inside it too (the same argument `subdivide_block` makes one level down);
* the land test — **no ring edge crossing the rectangle plus an inside centre
  means the whole rectangle is inland**, because a region whose boundary misses
  a connected set is either wholly in or wholly out of it. A corner test alone
  admits a block with a sea inlet through the middle of it, and
  `a_block_that_straddles_the_shore_is_refused` is the fixture that says so.

**The grid runs on the world axes**, and that is a stated bound rather than a
choice: a `PcgVolume` is a centre and an axis-aligned half-extent
(`GrammarContext` carries no rotation), so a settlement with its own bearing
needs either an oriented volume — an engine schema move — or one committed block
polygon per block, which is committing *geometry* where the small-committed-
folder law says commit *rules*.

**How the grid joins the island's road network.** It does not stitch anything:
`plan_network` routes **centre to centre**, so every highway and arterial that
reaches a settlement terminates at the site's own `(x, z)`, and the grid puts a
street line through that point on both axes. Measured: **22 route endpoints land
inside all 7 settlements, worst 2.000 m from a street centreline** against a
narrowest street reserve of 16 m — the arriving road ends on the carriageway it
hands over to. (The 2 m is the derivation lattice: the router works at 8 m and
the drape is at 1 m.)

**THE GRID LADDER, and the step it removed.** The first draft was one grid per
kind, and it made a settlement's existence a *step function of its radius*: a
city block's far corner is **155.6 m** from the crossroads, so a 150 m city
reservation held **zero** blocks and built nothing at all, silently. A
settlement takes the **coarsest grid of its kind's ladder that fits**
(`grid_for`), so the CI fixture's 120 m city takes the town's 76 m grid; a
reservation that fits neither builds nothing *and counts every cell it refused*.

**The zone library** is seven `.inf_pcg` documents in `samples/settlement/`,
**1 349–1 363 bytes each** — a footprint span over the volume's own extent,
IB-2c's subdivision, a palette choice. Engine content on the
`samples/ground` / `samples/starter-character` pattern: one copy, byte-locked
against its generator, named by both islands' recipes under `[content]` and by
every block's `PcgVolume.graph`. Committing a document per block would have been
committing geometry; **what makes 172 volumes 172 different blocks is the
seed.**

**AND THE SOURCE SCAN COULD NOT SEE A BRACE IMPORT.** `island.rs`'s
committed-design allowlist took the identifier after `inf_island::` and stopped,
so `use inf_island::{A, B};` read an **empty name and recorded nothing** — a
module importing every door in the crate on one line scanned clean. Found
because the settlement module's own anti-vacuity arm fired on its first run. The
extractor is shared now (`island::scan`), it reads brace groups, and **both**
modules run it.

### Clause 2 — the size raise, and the drift measured

Harbour City **520 → 600 m** (0.849 → **1.131 km²**) and Eastgate **480 → 570 m**
(0.724 → **1.020 km²**) — the brief of record's "≥ 1 km² each", and at a 120 m
block pitch the fourth ring the zoning table's House/Estate edge lives on. What
the wider pads moved, measured on the shipped island:

| | before (520/480) | after (600/570) |
|---|---|---|
| pad samples | 2 338 632 (2.339 km²) | **2 922 662 (2.923 km²), +25.0 %** |
| urban share of land | 5.8 % | **7.2 %** |
| reserved cells (8 m lattice) | 36 260 | **45 288, +24.9 %** |
| land / shore / peak | 40.653 km² / 25.14 km / 948.7 m | **all three unmoved** |
| reaches / lakes / waterfalls | 50 / 2 / 33 | **unmoved** |
| road grade audit | worst 0.118, 7 of 2 442 over | **bit-unmoved** |
| **stream drift** vs committed | 50 vs 51, **0.31 %** of length | 50 vs 51, **1.67 %** |
| **lake drift** | 2 vs 2, **16.47 %** of area | **16.47 %, unmoved** |
| detail band | 37 675 364 samples | 37 114 597 (the wider pad exclusion) |

**Then the re-derived layers are committed as the new design** — the I7
third-route precedent, and its carried remainder 6 closed. **51 reaches /
25.88 km and 2 lakes / 0.0847 km²** replace 50 / 26.32 km and 2 / 0.0708 km²;
the drift goes to **0.00 % / 0.00 %**; and the road audit **improves**: worst
0.118 → **0.108**, 7 over → **5 of 2 442** (0.29 % → 0.20 %).

**The fixture's camp grew and its town did not, and the difference is a
measurement.** `Fixture Camp` 90 → 130 m, because a 76 m town grid's first block
reaches 96.2 m and a 90 m reservation held zero. `Fixture Town` stays at 120 m,
because **a pad's rim is steeper than the hillside it is cut into by
construction**: `flatten_sample` eases with `smooth01`, whose derivative peaks at
1.5, so the rim's gradient is about **1.25× the local slope whatever the
radius**. Widening this pad walks that rim onto the road. Measured against a
0.100 ceiling on 144 stretches:

| Fixture Town radius | worst grade | stretches over |
|---|---|---|
| 120 m | **0.099** | **0** |
| 240 m | 0.110 | 1 |
| 280 m | 0.118 | 4 |
| 340 m | 0.125 | 5 — **3.47 %, BLOCKING** |

Re-planning the network first (`inf island route`) took 3.47 % to **3.08 %** and
no further. And past 140 m the pad fills this island's one lake and the derived
lake layer goes from one to none. So the recipe holds and the *generator* adapts
— which is where the grid ladder came from.

**The fixture's own water layers are NOT re-derived, and the refusal has its
number**: a fresh derivation finds 9 reaches of 1.33 km where the committed layer
has 9 of 1.25 km, and one of the new channels crosses a route — the audit goes
from **worst 0.099 / zero over to worst 0.239 / five**, because `carve_channels`
cuts a trench and this generator builds no bridges (the I7 refusal). The
committed layers stay and the drift stays at **5.43 %** of stream length with the
lake exact.

### Clause 3 — doors and enterability at settlement scale

`every_settlement_building_is_enterable` walks the hero to **each settlement in
turn** — they are kilometres apart and the partition holds one neighbourhood at
once, so "per settlement" is what that means — lets its cells activate,
re-derives every resident block's plans through `plans_of` (the same resolution
the shipped evaluation runs), and puts the three phase-19 invariants on each one
against **the solids the shipped world actually built**.

| settlement | buildings | storeys | flights | doorways | banded at 64 m |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture Town (city core: Hotel 4, Office 8, Shop 6) | 18 | 77 | 59 | 1 297 | 852 (**65.69 %**) |
| Fixture Camp (town: House 18, Shop 6) | 24 | 43 | 19 | 773 | 446 (**57.70 %**) |
| **total** | **42** | **120** | **78** | **2 070** | — |

The vacuity control comes with it: a slab through each building must read the
door **blocked**, or "no collider is in the void" is an assertion that cannot say
no (phase 19's own lesson, met at settlement scale).

**THE `is_open` WALK, RE-MEASURED — and the number that changed is the N, not the
constant.** The I6 audit found `door.is_open` walking all **19 790** doorways of
an *unstreamed* city to answer a question about one, and fixed it by checking the
reach before building a placement. On a streamed island the walk is over the
doorways the **simulation holds**: measured at **1 297 doorways over 4 resident
blocks, 21.3 µs a call beside a door and 21.8 µs a call five kilometres from
one** (~16 ns a doorway). The far call is not the dear one, which is the I6 fix
still holding, and the arm goes red if it stops.

**THE FURNISH BATTERY** (ruling 3: measure, then decide, default ON). One real
**100 × 100 m Harbour City block**, priced for **every archetype** rather than
for the one that happens to be zoned there — because `Shop` is one to two
storeys and `Hotel` is four to ten, furniture is per **room**, and a measurement
of the cheap one would have decided the ruling on the wrong building:

| archetype | storeys | buildings | doorways | bare solids | furnished | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Office | 3–8 | 9 | 776 | 13 960 | 16 228 | 1.16× |
| Apartment | 3–6 | 12 | 1 580 | 18 440 | 19 712 | 1.07× |
| Industrial | 1–2 | 4 | 27 | 1 023 | 1 465 | **1.43×** |
| House | 1–3 | 24 | 559 | 8 292 | 8 840 | 1.07× |
| Estate | 2–4 | 6 | 290 | 5 948 | 6 715 | 1.13× |
| Hotel | 4–10 | 9 | 2 462 | 30 561 | 33 446 | 1.09× |
| Shop | 1–2 | 20 | 266 | 5 721 | 6 212 | 1.09× |

**THE VERDICT, and it is not the one the ruling expected.** *Furnish is not what
costs.* Fully furnishing every resident block of the CI fixture's settlement
moves the fixed step **6.348 → 7.011 ms** (+0.663, +10.4 %) on 21 453 → 23 860
solids — while the *buildings themselves* are the other 6.3 ms.
*(I8a audit, MED-1: those two milliseconds are not reproducible — the arm runs a
wall clock inside a **parallel** test binary and the same comparison re-read
+0.821/+0.915/+0.805 ms alone, **−0.690 ms** with the whole file running, on an
identical world. The **counts** are exact on every machine and the verdict is
re-founded on them; the battery now carries an A/A′ noise floor. See the audit
ledger.)* The wave ships
`furnishes(a)` = **House, Shop, Estate**: the archetypes a player walks into on
foot, which are also the one-to-four-storey ones. The reasoning, stated so it can
be overturned with a number: the step is already at 97.6 % of its ratchet on the
real island *without* furniture, so spending 10 % more of a nearly-full budget on
rooms nobody has walked into is the wrong trade — not because furniture is
expensive, but because it is the only part of the bill that is optional today.

Load: build + cook of the whole fixture project, **1 573–2 376 ms** against a
5 000 ms `LOAD_BUDGET_MS`.

### Clause 4 — the gates and the budgets

**THE URBAN-BARE TRIPWIRE FLIPPED.** `island_gate.rs`'s
*"urban must stay bare for wave I8"* was an assertion about a wave that has now
happened. What is still true is that urban binds no **vegetation** graph, and the
reason is no longer "nobody has built the settlements yet" — it is that a
settlement is a `PcgVolume` in the LEVEL, not a biome binding, so the two
authorities never meet. Urban reserving the ground buys exactly what wave I7 said
it would: the generator finds bare ground rather than a forest to clear. The arm
asserts the settlements now — every block inside a reservation, every zone
document resolvable in the built project.

**AND THE GATE'S ZERO CONTROL STOPPED BEING ZERO, CORRECTLY.**
`the_biome_binding_scatters_when_its_ground_is_resident_and_not_before` asserted
that a world with cell streaming and no terrain streamer holds no tiles. It holds
one now, and the cause is IB-1's own rule that **PCG pages its own ground**: a
settlement block is a `Ground::Terrain` volume, so activating its cell pages the
page it needs. The true zero moved to a world with **neither** streamer (0 tiles,
0 instances); the cell-only world became what it is (**1 tile, 376 instances**
against the shipped boot's **16 and 14 636**). Likewise the scatter-mesh arm's
"one placeholder batch" is **nine** now, one per resident block — the claim was
never a count, it is that none carries geometry.

**THE NEW SETTLEMENT GATE.** `pie_equals_shipping_on_a_walk_into_a_building`:
enter the city, find a door, open it, step through, go upstairs — **123 steps,
123 DISTINCT states, byte-identical between the cooked pack and the loose
document.** Coverage first, on each host separately, because two empty worlds
agree perfectly: doorways resident, solids built, the door shut before and open
after, the doorway walkable, the first floor standable, the storey a real
**3.60 m**. The walk **discovers its own targets** — which door is nearest, which
building it belongs to, where that building's first floor is — so two hosts
holding different worlds disagree about the targets as well as about the folds.

Two findings inside it. **A door pressed from the LOCK SIDE while shut and
unlocked LOCKS rather than opens** ("locked from the inside" has to mean
something for whoever locked it), so the first draft stood on `prompt_position`,
pressed, and got a verdict that did not move: it had bolted the front door from
the hall. And **a stair core is full of treads at the floor above** — that is
what a flight IS — so a "no solid is here" test aimed at the core reads
blocked-by-2; the walk stands in the first non-stair room on floor one instead,
and the stair's own part is asserted as *reachability*.

**Mutation-verified**: deleting the settlement volumes from the level and
re-blessing kills **six of island_gate's twelve arms**, including all four new
ones.

**THE 900-STEP DRIVE, re-priced.** `pie_equals_shipping_on_an_island_drive` is
unmoved and green with the settlements standing: 900 steps, 900 distinct states,
byte-identical, and the drive now starts inside Fixture Town rather than on bare
ground. `city_scale` (11), `phase19_gate` (12) and `phase30_gameplay_gate` (6)
are all green and untouched.

**THE FIXED STEP, ON THE REAL ISLAND.** The instrument's island arm measures it
now, with the hero in Harbour City so the blocks around it are activated and
their parts banded:

> **5.853 ms/step against the 6.0 ms `CITY_STEP_BUDGET_MS` ratchet — INSIDE it,
> at 97.6 %.** 17 823 bodies, **17 289 ADMITTED structure colliders**, 58 582
> contact pairs (2 055 touching). `physics3d sync` 2.821 (48.2 %), `solver`
> 1.826 (31.2 %), `gameplay` 0.755 (12.9 %).

The ratchet is **not raised and not breached**. (The CI fixture's own settlement
reads 6.348 ms, over it, and that is a fact about the *fixture*: its 120 m
reservation takes the town's 76 m grid, so four blocks of city-core archetypes
sit inside one 64 m band. A number about a city has to come from a city, which is
why the instrument's arm exists.)

> **≥ 60 fps p50 `LIT+VIS` is NOT MET.** 106.221 ms against 16.6, where TER2b
> left 2.10 ms of headroom. This is the wave's headline and it is stated as a
> breach rather than a nuance.

**Read the per-pass GPU split WITHIN a run and not across the two**, which is
I4b's own law: the CPU frame went 6.3 → 63 ms between them, so `terrain`'s
2.077 → 15.788 is not a terrain regression — nothing about the terrain changed —
it is two different device states. Within the after-run the split is honest:
scatter 19.490, terrain 15.977, gi 3.465, vgeom 2.003.

**WHERE THE MILLISECONDS ARE, and what each one wants.** Three costs, three
mechanisms, three different owners:

1. **The projection: 20.2–21.7 ms against `PROJECTION_BUDGET_MS` = 1.5.** This is
   a **defect, not a content problem**. `push_pcg_scatter` rebuilds a volume's
   `loose` / `parts` / `shells` instance vectors **every frame** — 365 545
   `ScatteredInstance` copies, ~32 MB of memcpy at 60 Hz — for content that
   changes only when a cell activates. `PcgVolume::structures_gen` exists
   precisely to say "this did not change", and nothing on the projection path
   reads it. **The fix is Hardening Wave E's own pattern, one subsystem over**:
   `project_scene_full` already takes the *previous* frame's `RenderScene`, which
   is how terrain tiles are carried forward instead of deep-copied (6.370 →
   0.041 ms, 155×). Routed with its price: it takes the island's CPU frame from
   32.1 to ~13.4 ms, which is inside the 16.6 ms budget on its own. Not taken
   here because it edits a projector body pinned **character for character**
   between two hosts by `projector_mirror`, and that is a slice of its own.
   ***TAKEN BY THE I8a AUDIT*** (HIGH-1, `ScatterMemo`): projection **20.2 →
   0.631 ms shipped / 21.2 → 0.720 lit**, inside the 1.5 ms budget; SHIPPED p50
   **63.102 → 22.703 ms** and pipelined **32.057 → 11.740 (85.2 fps)**; LIT+VIS
   p50 **106.221 → 64.923** and pipelined **55.931 → 33.295 (30.0 fps)**. The
   routed ~13.4 was conservative. Post-fix tables in the audit ledger.
2. **The GPU: 30.4 ms shipped / 49.8 lit, of which scatter is 9.2 / 19.5.**
   *(I8a audit, MED-2: those numbers were taken from a run whose CPU was
   saturated by cost 1, which is the wave's own I4b law applied to itself. With
   the projection fixed the same flight reads GPU **11.740 shipped / 33.295 lit**
   and scatter **3.626 / 13.323** — the mechanism below is real and its
   magnitude was overstated by about 1.5×.)* This
   is the **path**, and it is the correction this wave makes to its own brief.
   The brief read *"the buildings are still cubes this slice, which is the cheap
   case"*. It is the **expensive** case: the settlements go through the P18.5 GPU
   **scatter** raster, which is a *foliage* path — no occlusion culling, no LOD
   below the per-building shell, and its instances here are not 0.3 m grass tufts
   but **wall-sized opaque boxes** that overdraw the screen many times over. The
   meshlet/vgeom path I8b is about already has the **two-pass HZB occlusion cull**
   P18 shipped and on by default. So *"a shipped city draws zero placeholder
   batches"* — I8b's own first requirement — is not a fidelity item. **It is the
   performance fix.**
3. **The fixed step: 5.853 ms, inside its ratchet**, and named here only so it is
   not mistaken for one of the two above.

**What was NOT done, and why.** Thinning the settlements was priced and refused:
to bring 365 545 instances inside the frame by design numbers alone needs a **10×
cut** — one or two buildings per 100 m block at one or two storeys — which is a
suburb, not a city, and it would trade a measured engine defect for a permanently
worse world. Cutting `ISLAND_ACTIVATION_M` 256 → 128 was priced too (~2.8× fewer
resident blocks) and refused for a different reason: cell activation is what
*spawns* the entities, so a shorter radius means distant districts do not exist
to draw their shells, and a city you cannot see from 300 m is not a city.

**0 blocks were refused off-land** on either island — every reservation the

**What a block becomes**, from the battery's own 100 × 100 m Harbour City block:
between **1 023 solids** (Industrial, 4 buildings) and **30 561** (Hotel, 9
buildings), averaging ~12 000. **The resident set at Harbour City is 365 545

**WHAT DRAWS: STILL CUBES.** Every one of the 365 545 is a `PrimMesh::Cube`
tinted from `kind_index`. **I8b's first requirement is named here and it is not
what it looks like: *a shipped city draws zero placeholder batches* is the
PERFORMANCE clause of that wave, not its fidelity clause** — see cost 2 above.

**Carried, by name:**

1. **≥ 60 fps p50 LIT+VIS is not met and the island is at 9.4 fps.** The
   headline. Three costs, three mechanisms, all three above. *(I8a audit: after
   HIGH-1 it is **15.4 fps p50 / 30.0 fps pipelined**. Still not met, and it is
   still the headline.)*
2. **The projection breaches `PROJECTION_BUDGET_MS` (1.5) at 20.2 ms**, with the
   fix and its price stated. This is the one an implementer can take tomorrow.
   *(I8a audit: **CLOSED**, HIGH-1 — 0.631 ms shipped / 0.720 lit.)*
3. **The settlement streets are a PLAN, not a surface.** They decide where the
   blocks are and they carry the join to the island road network; they are not
   drawn. The island's road mesh is draped at the *terrain's* pitch (1 m) because
   a road over real ground has chord error at any coarser step, and
   `roads::build_mesh` takes **one** `ground_step_m` for one layer — while a
   settlement street sits on a levelled pad, where the chord error is
   **0.000000 m at any step** (the `phase30-city` measurement). Drawing them
   honestly wants a *second* surface at a coarse step. At the island's 1 m pitch
   the grid is **60.88 km** of centreline, which at a 7 m single-carriageway
   width is ~426 000 m² and would roughly double the road mesh's 517 086
   vertices. Routed beside I8b's sidewalk/kerb item.
4. **A settlement's grid runs on the world axes.** No bearing per site — see
   clause 1 for the two costs of giving it one.
5. **`ISLAND_ACTIVATION_M` puts a whole city in memory at once.** 256 m
   activation + 256 m prefetch over a 600 m city is ~25 cells and ~30 blocks
   resident. That is what makes 365 545 instances a *per-frame* number; it is
   also what makes the city visible. Both halves are above.
6. **The fixture's water layers drift 5.43 %** and are deliberately not
   re-derived (a new channel crosses a route and there are no bridges).
7. **The fixture's own settlement step is 6.348 ms**, over the ratchet, because
   its 120 m reservation packs four city-core blocks into one 64 m band. A
   fixture is not a city. *(I8a audit: nor is 6.348 a number — the same world
   reads 8.1–8.2 ms with the arm alone and 10.7 ms with the file's other eleven
   arms on other threads. What is over the ratchet is not in doubt; the figure
   is. MED-1.)*
8. **`inf island build`'s default output for the CI fixture lands INSIDE the
   tree** (`samples/island-fixture/project`), because that recipe's
   `[source] cache` is `tiles/` beside itself and the default out is
   `cache_dir()/../project`. Gitignored; the gate builds into a temp dir and
   never touches it.
9. **The vacuous-by-construction half of the `is_open` walk**: the arm bounds the
   far call against the near one, which catches the reach check being lost, and
   does **not** bound either against an absolute microsecond figure, because a
   microsecond is a fact about the machine.
